risks.note: Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Malware, social engineering and software supply-chain attacks create a high risk of theft of sensitive customer data, which the company describes as both a data-privacy and a reputational risk. Mitigations cited are disk encryption, disablement of USB and a cyber security and data privacy policy; the Risk Management Committee reviews cyber security within the ERM framework.

Identified as a material risk with negative financial implications. Low employee motivation is said to lead to decreased productivity, higher absenteeism, increased turnover, compromised work quality and reputational damage. The BRSR reports a permanent-employee turnover rate of 59% total in FY 2025-26 against 51% in FY 2024-25 and 14% in FY 2023-24, on a permanent employee base of 102 — attrition is structurally high and rising on a very small workforce.

The BRSR reports that education services account for 100.00% of turnover, split between Education Support Service (38.43%) and Other Education (61.57%), with no exports (0.00% of turnover). Earnings depend entirely on one sector and on the domestic market.

The BRSR reports operations in only 6 states nationally with zero plants and two offices, and no international locations, so the business is concentrated in a small number of Indian states even as the company aspires to reach every district headquarters.

The BRSR states that SEIL's customers include franchisees and that the company focuses on operations through franchisees for preschools, K-12 schools and higher studies, and that it does not have a direct workforce but engages workers through contracted services. Delivery quality, brand consistency and revenue therefore depend on third parties SEIL does not directly employ or control.

The Board-approved Scheme of Arrangement — slump sale of the education undertaking to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited followed by amalgamation of SEIL with GREW Energy Private Limited — remains subject to approvals from shareholders, creditors, the Stock Exchanges, the jurisdictional NCLT and other regulators. Non-receipt or delay would leave shareholders holding a materially different asset than the one contemplated, and the transaction redirects SEIL shareholders' exposure from education to solar PV manufacturing.

currentContext.expansion: SEIL's expansion is footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-led: the BRSR reports zero plants and two offices nationally, and the company describes an asset-light core with 350+ preschool centres across 74+ cities and an in-house uniform manufacturing facility. Stated forward initiatives are to strengthen and scale the six existing brands, expand Catalyzer's consultancy and institutional training to a broader base of institutions and corporate clients, build structured corporate learning and workforce-training programmes, provide end-to-end school management systems, launch an online courses and certification portfolio, offer career counselling and placement support for higher education institutions, and introduce a fully integrated technology-enabled distribution platform for uniforms and accessories under UniformVerse building on the School Shack online store. The company also states it will continue its push to establish a presence in every district headquarters in India, and lists integration of smart-classroom and digital learning technologies among its core focus areas. No timelines or rupee quantum are attached to any of these initiatives. Separately, on 2nd March 2026 the Boards approved a two-step Scheme of Arrangement: SEIL's business undertaking is transferred to Shanti Learning Initiatives Private Limited by slump sale, after which SEIL amalgamates with GREW Energy Private Limited (a Chiripal Group solar PV manufacturer operating a 6.5 GW module plant at Dudu, Rajasthan and setting up 8.0 GW of solar cells at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, of which 3.0 GW are already operational), with GREW Energy to be listed on a recognised stock exchange upon all approvals. Those solar capacities belong to GREW Energy, the counterparty, not to SEIL. BRSR Principle 2 reports NIL R&D and NIL capex investments in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
